prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One of the eight angles formed measures $115°$. What is the measure, in degrees, of an angle that is supplementary to it?
hint: When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, every angle is either equal to $115°$ or supplementary to it.

hints.text: When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, every angle is either equal to $115°$ or supplementary to it.

learningObjective: Use the two-angle structure formed by a transversal across parallel lines.
explanation: A transversal crossing two parallel lines creates only two distinct angle measures, and they are supplementary.
One is $115°$, so the other is $180 - 115 = 65°$.
Four of the eight angles measure $115°$ and the other four measure $65°$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Only two numbers exist in the figure
steps: Rather than memorizing "corresponding", "alternate interior", and "co-interior" separately, notice that every angle is one of just two values.
Angles that look equal are equal; angles that look different are supplementary.
With parallel lines, the picture is reliable in exactly this one respect — and it collapses eight angle names into one idea.
